review_scope: Independent fresh-context review of K4 only; no prior review reports or implementation inspected.

comprehension.claim: Reusing physical storage preserves initialized logical byte values when competing object/generation lifetimes are ordered on every admitted execution, initialization and language validity are preserved, and all readers including recovery readers are modeled.
comprehension.induction: Matched initialization establishes the invariant for initialized bytes of live objects. Matched writes preserve the target byte and cannot change another live overlapping object under assumption 2; reads return the invariant value. Allocation extends the invariant only for initialized bytes after prior occupants become inaccessible, and release removes its object. Finite-prefix induction covers accesses at arbitrary finite positions of ongoing executions.
comprehension.generations_and_in_place: The general theorem conservatively excludes overlapping whole-object generations. The in-place specialization instead requires a per-read version argument: for a byte invalidated by overwrite, every subsequent read must target its current new version or an independently preserved old copy. This needs a byte/version availability invariant rather than literal simultaneous equality for all bytes of obsolete generations. The text explicitly requests per-read version induction, which supplies this specialization under the surrounding matched-access model.
comprehension.concurrency_and_recovery: All-execution lifetime ordering and the explicit ordered-access/synchronization premise prevent selecting a convenient schedule as proof. Fault handlers, interrupts, serialization, retained pointers and recovery readers participate in the modeled lifetime. The rollback example correctly invalidates reuse based only on successful-path liveness.
comprehension.counterexample_search: Considered partial initialization, live overlapping generations, delayed interrupt/rollback reads, stale pointers after release, concurrent read/write overlap, and old-version reads after in-place overwrite. Each value-corruption case violates an explicit premise or the specialization read condition. Observable addresses, invalid C provenance/aliasing and newly introduced faults are outside the theorem unless separately matched; they are not established by this abstract induction.

remaining_application_obligations: Define the actual logical objects, generations, byte mappings, initialization events and admitted executions; prove capacity, alignment, C type/provenance/aliasing validity and initialization for every read, including any padding accessed by serialization.

Establish lifetime separation for every admitted normal, fault, interrupt and recovery execution, including retained pointers, deferred operations and backup readers; successful-path last-use analysis is insufficient.
Justify the concurrency premise with actual synchronization or a defined ordered-access semantics; the abstract proof is not a C memory-model or hardware/DMA proof.
For each in-place operation, establish the intended version of every read and continued availability of independently retained old copies after every overwrite, including fault/recovery reads.
Match any observable pointer/address identities, timing and other external effects required by the interface; separately address new faults, corruption and resource exhaustion.
Retain complete resource accounting for stack, scratch, registry metadata, padding, backups and cache payloads; this proof does not establish an SRAM bound or firmware readiness.
